newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MITI panel urges bold financial reforms.
newsitem.headline: Japan MITI panel urges bold financial reforms.

text.p: Japan must carry out sweeping financial reforms if it is to avoid a "hollowing out" of its financial markets, an advisory panel to the trade minister said on Wednesday.

Such reforms should be implemented before the new Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Law becomes effective in April 1998, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry's (MITI) subcommittee for industrial finance said in an interim report.
The forex law revision will remove barriers to cross-border financial transactions. Without drastic reforms, Japan may risk losing financial businesses to overseas markets, the panel said.

The panel said financial laws needed for Japan's "Big Bang" reforms should be enacted by the early part of fiscal year 1999/2000, which begins on April 1, 1999. Japan aims to liberalise its financial markets by 2001 in a "Big Bang" deregulation plan to catch up with reforms carried out more than a decade ago in Europe and North America. The following are the main points of the panel's proposals:
-Japan needs to carry out sweeping financial deregulation before the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Law becomes effective in April 1988.
-Japan needs to enact the laws and legal framework necessary for the "Big Bang" reforms by early 1999/2000.
-Full liberalisation of brokerage commissions should be implemented in view of the foreign exchange law revision in April 1998.
-Japan must scrap its securities transactions tax, now imposed on all transactions in securities, so it can compete fairly with overseas markets.
-Japan needs to review its withholding tax in order to encourage bond purchases by non-residents of Japan.
-Competition in the financial industry should be increased by allowing easier entrance by new players.
-Full deregulation should be implemented to allow banks, securities houses, trust banks and insurance firms to enter each others' business areas.
-Japan needs to develop an environment in which securitisation of assets can be carried out smoothly.
-Japan should introduce a Japanese government bond (JGB) with a five-year maturity which could be used as a benchmark for the medium-term debt sector.
-Japan should ensure a channel through which money can flow into venture capital firms via deregulation in such fields as investment trusts.
-Japan should drastically streamline public financial institutions and limit their role to needs which cannot be met by the private sector or the capital markets.

-Japan should examine the current portofolios of public financial bodies. Thirty percent of the total issue amount of JGBs and some 60 percent of municipal debt are currently held by public financial institutions. While this enables smooth sales of public debt, it also distorts interest rate formation across the yield curve.
Smooth public debt sales are also weakening the financial discipline of public debt issuers, including the government and municipal governments.
